summary: Feed s153_double to IDS is degraded: 51.8% of TCP sessions are one-way and 16.9% of frames are sliced to 256 bytes. IDS requires bidirectional traffic and full payload for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction of traffic. 103 of 199 TCP sessions (51.8%) show only one side, well above 10% threshold. Typical cause is SPAN configured as TX or RX only, ingress-only TAP, or broker policy/filter that does not aggregate both directions of a flow to the same IDS tool port, or asymmetric routing where only one path is tapped.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, flow state tracking and signature correlation. With half the sessions one-way, the IDS cannot validate handshakes, track state, or detect bidirectional exploits, causing missed detections and inaccurate alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port so the IDS sees client->server and server->client together for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/packet trimming is enabled and cutting frames to ~256 bytes. 391 of 2319 frames (16.9%) are truncated, exceeding 5% threshold. This is a broker optimization to save bandwidth but removes L7 payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection and signature matching. Truncation at 256 bytes strips HTTP bodies, exploit payloads, and file transfers, so IDS will miss payload-based attacks and cannot perform full stream reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing/trimming for this IDS feed so full packets are delivered; IDS cannot detect threats without complete payload. If bandwidth is constrained, use filtering instead of slicing.
